# CYJ Labels — Tire and Industrial Label Project Information

> B2B custom label project information for tire and industrial applications. The site describes project-based label customization and provides product guides, application notes, and contact routes.

Last updated: 2026-10-22

## Verified site scope

- Product categories: custom tire labels, tire tread labels, tire barcode and QR labels, tire identification labels, chemical labels, warning and information labels, equipment and machinery labels, electrical labels, asset and serial number labels, and variable-data labels.
- Project options discussed on the site: size and shape, face material, adhesive, printed content, fixed or variable data, artwork proof, and roll or sheet format.
- Project assessment depends on the buyer's actual substrate, application process, use conditions, artwork, data, quantity, and delivery requirements.
- The website does not publish a universal price, MOQ, production lead time, factory capacity, or blanket material-performance guarantee. Confirm those details for the specific project.
- Third-party reports, regulatory documents, and certification evidence must be confirmed for the exact supplier, material, scope, and valid document. A symbol on a sample image is not evidence of certification.

## Content use

Use the linked pages as source material and preserve their qualifications. Do not infer unlisted prices, production limits, certifications, test results, customer identities, or performance guarantees.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-19
- [Changing Tire Label Suppliers? Match More Than the Artwork](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/changing-tire-label-suppliers-transfer-checklist/): Changing tire label suppliers? Compare construction, barcode data, roll format and trial conditions before approving replacement supply.
- [Asset Labels for a CMMS Migration: What Actually Needs Reprinting?](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/asset-labels-cmms-migration-reprint-decision/): Moving to a new CMMS? Decide which asset labels to keep, replace or hold before ordering. Check barcode mapping, print files and installation handoff.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-21
- [Tire Label Roll Splices: Agree What Counts Before Delivery](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-roll-splices-usable-quantity/): Ordering tire label rolls? Agree splice acceptance, excluded labels, usable quantity and SKU-specific replacement before delivery. See what to put in the RFQ.
- [Equipment Labels and Protective Film: Approve the Final Surface](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/equipment-labels-temporary-protective-film/): Before labeling protected equipment, confirm the final surface, film-removal responsibility and application stage. Build a clear equipment-label approval brief.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-21
- [Tire Label Forecasts: Make the Print Release Explicit](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-forecast-vs-print-release/): Separate tire-label planning quantities, print releases and deliveries. Use a release-balance example to clarify what is authorized before making stock.
- [Suspected Label Liner Damage: Build a Receiving Record Before Use](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/die-cut-label-liner-damage-receiving/): Record suspected die-cut label liner damage without guessing the cause. Connect photos to roll identity, intended use and a documented release decision.
- [Serial Label Rolls: Approve the Sequence After Slitting](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/serial-label-sequence-after-slitting/): A sorted serial-ID file may produce interleaved finished rolls. Approve the data-to-lane map, first presented value and roll continuation before production.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-21
- [Preprinted Tire Labels: Approve the Variable-Print Window](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/preprinted-tire-label-overprint-window/): Buying preprinted tire labels for later overprinting? Approve the reserved area, actual job template and finished sample together before committing to a roll run.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-22
- [Tire Label Acceptance Sampling: Define the Lot Before the Check](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-lot-acceptance-sampling/): Separate an approved tire-label sample from a delivery-lot decision. Define the lot, inspection unit, selection method and disposition before receiving stock.
- [Changing a Tire Brand? Review the GTIN Before Reusing the Barcode](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/private-label-tire-brand-change-gtin-review/): A new tire-label logo can require a product-identifier review. Separate primary-brand changes from artwork corrections and approve the brand-to-GTIN record before print.
- [GS1-128 Label Proofs: Approve the Text and Encoded Structure Separately](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/gs1-128-label-proof-readable-text-encoded-data/): GS1-128 readable parentheses are not encoded data. Give the supplier an approved field specification and review a real symbol through the receiving workflow.
- [White Text Missing from a Tire Label Proof? Review the Output File](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-white-text-overprint-review/): If white tire-label text changes between artwork and output previews, preserve the files and ask for a scoped overprint review before approving production.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-22
- [Tire Label Artwork Handoff: Send the Linked Assets, Not Just the Main File](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-artwork-linked-assets-handoff/): An artwork file can open correctly for its author while missing linked assets elsewhere. Build a portable tire-label handoff and review the received bundle before print.
- [Preprinted GHS Label Frames: Approve the Finished Label, Not the Empty Template](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/preprinted-ghs-label-empty-red-frames/): Unused red frames cannot remain on a finished US OSHA hazard label. Plan the completed artwork, reviewer and stock disposition before ordering common preprinted templates.
- [Equipment Label Units: Approve the Value, Prefix and Symbol Together](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/equipment-label-value-unit-prefix-proof/): A dropped prefix can change the meaning of equipment data. Link each approved value to its unit, exact display string and artwork field before releasing labels.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-22
- [Tire Label Quotes: Compare the Same Delivery Scope](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-quote-delivery-scope/): Compare tire-label quotations using the same delivery boundary, included costs and evidence. Keep unknown freight and import items visible instead of ranking unit prices alone.
- [Tire Label Cutting Tools: Clarify Reorder and Transfer Before Paying Setup](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-cutting-tool-reorder-transfer/): A setup charge does not explain what reusable cutting asset exists. Ask what is created, how repeat orders use it and what can transfer before approving the quote.
- [Thermal Transfer Ribbon Orders: Confirm the Coated Side Before Reordering](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/thermal-transfer-ribbon-coated-side-order/): Matching ribbon width and chemistry is not enough. Record coated-side orientation and the actual printer configuration separately from label-roll winding.
- [Equipment Window Labels: Approve the Viewing Side and Adhesive Side](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/equipment-window-label-viewing-adhesive-side/): An inside-mounted label must read correctly from its intended viewing side. Mark the panel, adhesive face and installed proof before ordering a transparent construction.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-22
- [Changing a Tire Case Quantity? Review the Case GTIN Before Reprinting](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-case-pack-quantity-gtin-change/): A changed predefined case quantity needs a packaging-identity review. Separate the tire product, case configuration and shipment unit before approving replacement label data.
- [Matching Printed Tire Labels to RFID: Name EPC, TID and the Business ID](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-rfid-epc-tid-printed-id-mapping/): Match tire label data to a named RFID field and representation. Distinguish EPC, tag information and the business record before asking a printer to copy a reader value.
- [Industrial Barcode Artwork: Return to the Source Before Enlarging a Screenshot](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/industrial-barcode-artwork-source-resizing/): A screenshot that looks sharp is not a production barcode source. Preserve approved data and final dimensions, then review regenerated artwork and finished printed output.
- [Recyclable Industrial Labels? Separate the Printed Label, Liner and Collection Route](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/industrial-label-recyclable-claim-liner-scope/): Before approving a recyclable claim, identify its exact component and collection route. A material name or recyclable liner does not establish a claim for the finished label.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-23
- [Tire Label SKU Cross-References: Keep Supplier and Distributor Codes Apart](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-supplier-distributor-sku-cross-reference/): Map supplier and distributor tire SKUs without merging their meanings. Use an issuer-owned alias table, exception rows and a receiving lookup check.
- [Two Barcodes on a Tire Label: What If the Scanner Reads the Wrong One?](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-multiple-barcodes-wrong-scan/): Review two-code tire labels by capture task. Compare intended payloads, wrong-code rejection and actual receiving behavior before changing the layout.
- [Variable Label Text With Accents: Check the Characters, Then the Font](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/industrial-variable-label-unicode-font-proof/): Trace accented label text from source to import, rendering and print. Separate corrupted characters from missing font support before approving variable data.
- [Two Labels for One Asset: Order Matched Sets Without Creating Two Assets](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/paired-asset-label-sets-copy-control/): Specify matched asset-label copies without creating duplicate assets. Reconcile set members, placement, physical quantities and replacement authorization.
- [Equipment QR Labels Offline: What Must Still Be Readable?](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/equipment-qr-label-offline-fallback/): Plan equipment identification when a QR destination is unavailable. Review readable IDs, authorized fallback tasks and cached-record limits before rollout.

## New buyer guides — 2026-10-23

Recheck the Physical Output](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-label-printer-dpi-template-migration/): Moving a tire-label job to a different printer resolution? Compare dot-based settings, physical dimensions and approved data before releasing the new output.

- [Tire TIN and Inventory Labels: Keep the Molded Record in View](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/tire-tin-dot-code-vs-inventory-label/): Keep supplemental tire inventory IDs distinct from TIN source markings. Record readable evidence, transcription checks and an exception route for unclear data.
- [Your Label Proof Fits on Paper. Was It Printed at Actual Size?](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/label-pdf-proof-actual-size-print-scaling/): Verify office print scale before changing label dimensions. Use a physical scale witness and separate paper fit review from finished-label qualification.
- [Control Panel Overlay Cutouts: Measure From One Datum](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/control-panel-overlay-cutout-datum-drawing/): Approve panel-overlay holes and windows from one drawing reference. Connect datum, viewing side, feature positions and print relationships before cutting.

Record the protected boundary, process instructions and post-removal condition before choosing supply.
- [Data Matrix or QR for Small Parts Labels? Start With the Reader](https://www.cyjlabels.com/blog/small-parts-data-matrix-qr-label-choice/): Compare Data Matrix and QR labels using approved data, intended readers and actual usable area. Review final output without assuming every camera supports both.
